video.title: I Asked AI to Help Me Beat the Stock Market

summary: Chris Koerner shows how he vibe-coded a stock portfolio backtesting app in Replit (Agent 3) to test his thesis that founder-led S&P 500 companies with strong network effects beat the market. He used ChatGPT deep research to find candidates, then built a live Google Sheet using the GOOGLEFINANCE formula, and used GPT for Sheets to score every S&P 500 company 1-10 on network effects and founder leadership for about $15 in credits. Replit then turned the sheet into a filterable dashboard. On his 8-10/8-10 filter over 10 years he reports 22.4% vs the S&P's 9% weighted and 12% unweighted. He shares about a dozen ChatGPT prompts for generating stock-picking theses and says he put the free tool ("Nel Stocks") behind an email form on a domain he bought. The business angle is small: a free, email-gated vibe-coded tool used as a lead magnet. Most of the video is personal investing, not a business.

ideas.name: Free vibe-coded niche tool gated behind an email form (lead magnet)
ideas.one_liner: Build a niche data tool quickly with an AI coding agent, put it on its own domain, and give it away in exchange for an email address.
ideas.business_model: Free tool as an audience and email-list builder; no monetisation stated
ideas.customer: Retail investors interested in stock-picking frameworks
ideas.problem: Retail investors lack an easy way to backtest a simple thesis against the S&P 500
ideas.offer: Free web app (Nel Stocks) that filters S&P 500 companies by network-effect and founder-led scores and charts returns vs the index

pricing.notes: Host says there is nothing to pay for; you just enter your email.

acquisition_channels.details: Tool promoted in the host's video; access requires email sign-up.

ideas.delivery: Replit Agent 3 app reading a live Google Sheet (GOOGLEFINANCE prices, GPT for Sheets 1-10 scores). Built in about 45 minutes of prompting.
unit_economics_claims: About $15 of GPT for Sheets credits to score all S&P 500 companies
About 45 minutes of prompting to build the app
ideas.startup_cost: About $15 AI credits plus a domain and Replit plan (not quantified)

acquisition.how: Inbound from content; the email gate captures leads automatically. Any later marketing emails need consent under UK PECR (opt-in at sign-up).

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK, but investment tools risk FCA financial-promotion and advice rules if they recommend stocks. Keep it educational with disclaimers. Email capture needs UK GDPR consent, and PECR consent for marketing emails.

risks: Backtests are survivorship-biased (current S&P 500 constituents) and incomplete (missing IPO data)
Could be seen as investment advice or a financial promotion

tactics.name: Use GPT for Sheets to score a list at scale
steps: Put the entity names in a Google Sheet column
Write a prompt with a 1-10 rubric that references the cell
Drag the formula down the whole column
Use the scores as filterable data in an app

quote.text: I had a prompt that said tell me on a scale of 1 to 10 and then I inserted the name of the company how much in this case Kagra Brands enjoys network effects.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Point a vibe-coded app at a live Google Sheet and define every column
steps: Start with a hardcoded spreadsheet upload for a rough draft
Replace it with an editable live Google Sheet link as the database
Explain what each column means rather than letting the AI guess
Request formatting fixes and a visible list of filtered rows to check the math

quote.text: Now, it can surmise what each column means, but I don't want to assume that it knows. I would rather get ahead of it, take a few more extra minutes
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: The backtest uses today's S&P 500 constituents (survivorship bias) and is not investment advice; this is an extractor note, not said in the video.

lessons.lesson: Give the AI coding agent explicit definitions of your data rather than letting it infer them; it reduces errors.

quote.text: I told it what each column meant. Now, it can surmise what each column means, but I don't want to assume that it knows.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Newer agents (Replit Agent 3) test and fix their own builds, removing much of the prompt-debug loop.

quote.text: it will start stress testing your tool, breaking it, fixing it, breaking it, fixing it, all while you just sit there and wait.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: AI-in-spreadsheet tools let you turn fuzzy judgements into numeric scores across hundreds of rows cheaply.

quote.text: You can basically use any AI tool inside of a Google sheet.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Ask the app to show the underlying rows so you can verify the filtering and the maths.

quote.text: I wanted to check the math of the chart and show me the stocks at the bottom of all this so I can make sure that it was filtering correctly.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A quick free tool on its own domain can double as an email list builder.
Look for mismatches between fundamentals and price, such as a company holding more cash than its market value.

quote.text: Coinbase had more cash on their balance sheet than they were worth as a company. That's a fact.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand, screen-shared build with specific cost and time figures, but the return figure is a hobbyist backtest with survivorship bias and missing data. The business element is a minor aside with no revenue.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes Replit (a frequent tool of the host) and the host's own email-gated site.
